name: scroll-pageup-third-press
opens_with: The long transcript at 80x24, then THREE pageups — the third-press ladder rung
notes: The 80x24 third-press variant of scroll-pageup-moves-viewport, split out by the tui-bugfix campaign's corpus repair. History: iter-1200 added this variant to pin the third press (the iter-1192 residual threw the reader back to the tail on press three — mutation-proven by restoring the pre-fix arithmetic and watching exactly this variant fail with the same 'expected to contain L061'); iter-1213 corrected the base notes' harness-blink to the real root cause (PgUp was focus-gated; it is unconditional now). **RE-GATED in iter-1751.** The variant used to carry `deterministic: false` because its landing line moved with the machine's load: the keys arrived before the mock transcript landed, and the plain `--dump-screen` path paints the frame BEFORE the last key is applied (the base scenario's notes measured this: 'the plain path coalesces and the final state never lands'), so the dumped frame was a race. The harness now has the token the notes asked for — `<wait:N>` in the key sequence, N IDLE FRAMES with no key applied (frames, not milliseconds: a frame count is deterministic by construction, a duration would put the verdict back on the machine's load) — so the content lands before the presses and the final frame settles. The landing is now machine-stable, so this scenario carries its landing assert and its goldens again instead of the state asserts alone. Method note for whoever mutates this next: the runner never builds, so `_run.py` must be preceded by `scripts/build.sh` or the mutation is silently ignored and the run "passes" against the stale binary.
